transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. Nice to meet you too. Well, I came in because things have been really extreme for me lately at work. 

I went from just... launching nonstop plant redesign projects, calling our suppliers way after hours, and basically rewriting the whole shift plan by myself, to suddenly being completely unable to keep up with the very plans I had just set in motion. It's just really overwhelming, and I need to figure out what's going on with me.
During the time when you were launching all those projects and calling suppliers after hours, were you needing much less sleep than usual?

Yeah, definitely. I was sleeping maybe two or three hours a night during that stretch. But I wasn't tired at all—I'd still show up at the plant the next morning feeling completely sharp and charged. It honestly just felt like sleep was optional, or kind of an inefficient use of my time with everything I had going on.
During that high-energy stretch, did you feel unusually confident or powerful, like you could do things other people couldn’t?

Yes, definitely. I mean, I honestly believed I could fix the entire production workflow by myself, and do it faster than the whole consulting team we had brought in. Whenever anyone brought up concerns or tried to slow me down, I just brushed them off. It really just felt like failure didn't even seem possible to me at the time.
During that high-energy period, did you have any beliefs that others said were unrealistic or not true?

No, I don't think so. I mean... people definitely told me my timelines were impossible, or that I was taking on way too much at once. But they never said the things I was talking about were actually untrue or completely out of touch with reality. It was all real work stuff for the plant, I just... I just thought I could execute it all perfectly and way faster than anyone else.
During that high-energy period, were you hospitalized because of your behavior?

No, I wasn't. I mean... I was definitely intense and probably pretty difficult to work with during that time, but it never got to a point where I had to go to a hospital or anything like that. I was really just going back and forth between my house and the plant.
About how many days did that high-energy stretch last?

I'm not exactly sure how many days it was, to be honest. I didn't really keep track. It just felt like a continuous blur of working and going back and forth to the plant. I'd have to really think back to figure out the exact number of days.
During that high-energy stretch, did your behavior cause serious problems at work or in your life?

No, not really. I wouldn't say it caused any serious problems. I mean, my coworkers were definitely annoyed with how intense I was being at the plant, and I was probably exhausting to be around. But I didn't get in trouble with management or put my job in jeopardy or anything like that. I was actually getting a ton of work done, so it didn't really negatively impact my life in a major way, if that's what you mean.
Did that high-energy period last at least 4 days?
Yeah, it definitely lasted at least four days. Like I said, I'm not sure the exact number, but it was for sure longer than that. It was a solid stretch of just... going non-stop.
After that high-energy period ended, did you have a stretch of at least two weeks where you felt depressed or down most of the day nearly every day?

Yeah, I did. Actually, it's been going on for a while now. Lately, I wake up in my temporary apartment and just have this heavy, hollow feeling. It's like... the day is already ruined before I even get in the car to drive to the plant. And that feeling just kind of stays with me most of the day, pretty much every day.
During this depressed period, have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

No, not really. I mean, I don't think so. I still do the things I normally do, like watching TV after work or reading a bit. I wouldn't say I've stopped enjoying them, it's just... everything feels heavier right now. But the interest is still there.
During this down period, has your appetite changed noticeably?

Yeah, my eating is kind of all over the place right now. Um, some days I'll be at the plant and suddenly realize it's 4 p.m. and all I've had is coffee. But then other nights, I'll just stand in the kitchen at my apartment and eat takeout straight from the container, even if I'm not actually hungry. It's just very inconsistent.
During this down period, have you had thoughts that you would be better off dead or of hurting yourself?

No, I haven't had any thoughts like that. Um, even though things feel really heavy and exhausting right now, I don't want to hurt myself. I definitely haven't thought about being better off dead or anything.
During this down period, have you been feeling unusually tired or low on energy?

No, I wouldn't say I'm unusually tired. My energy levels are actually pretty normal. I know I said earlier that things feel heavy right now, but I still have the physical energy to get through my shifts at the plant and do what I need to do. I'm not, you know, physically drained or struggling to get out of bed or anything like that.
